extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in media criticism, journalism professionals, and advocates for press accountability
extracted.subtask_description: A news piece reporting on a letter from journalism professors urging The New York Times to investigate and publicly report on alleged failures in reporting, editing, and publishing a specific article about October 7 sexual violence. The piece summarizes allegations, prior reporting, and calls for transparency and corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission independent review of reporting, editing, and publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Times must 'immediately commission a group of journalism experts to conduct a thorough and full independent review of the reporting, editing and publishing processes for this story and release a report of the findings.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a direct demand from the professors' letter cited in the article. The review should be independent, thorough, cover reporting/editing/publishing workflows, and culminate in a publicly released findings report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to standards for evidence and fact-gathering
rubrics_metrics.description: The story allegedly 'didn't meet the paper’s standards for evidence and fact-gathering.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cites internal NYT questioning of the reporting and outside investigations that raised concerns. Journalistic practice should ensure claims—especially serious allegations—are supported by verifiable evidence before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid publishing questionable or fabricated claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports have found that the claims in the paper’s article are 'questionable, if not fabricated.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Intercept and other reporting highlighted problems with the factual basis of the piece. Newsrooms should verify source material and avoid amplifying unsubstantiated or fabricated accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper vetting and oversight of freelance contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Scrutinize the contributions and methods of freelancers and non-staff sources, given that at least one person 'had no previous reporting experience' and gathered evidence in a 'highly questionable process.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article highlights Anat Schwartz’s role and lack of reporting experience; news organizations should vet freelancers' methods, corroborate their information independently, and ensure they meet reporting standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use precise language to distinguish allegations from proven facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid treating allegations as established facts—Jeffrey Gettleman reportedly said he didn’t 'want to even use the word evidence' because of its legal connotations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters and editors should clearly label what is alleged versus corroborated, and not downplay the difference between unverified claims and proven evidence in headlines and framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate and publicly address grave reporting errors using precedent
rubrics_metrics.description: Past examples (The Times' Jayson Blair investigation; Rolling Stone's probe and retraction) show that news organizations should investigate serious errors and publicly account for them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The professors invoke historical precedents to argue for a formal investigation and public report when reporting failures of this magnitude occur; follow-through and transparency are part of remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider and disclose real-world harms and impacts of reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how reporting affects affected communities—the professors argue the story 'has had an immeasurable effect on Palestinians' and 'fueled the fire' during wartime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsrooms should evaluate potential harms their reporting may cause (especially in conflict contexts) and factor impact into editorial decisions and corrective actions; disclosure of harms should be part of any remedial report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against editorial bias or slanted framing
rubrics_metrics.description: The article reports that the story 'served to boost the paper’s pro-Israel slant,' implying a failure to maintain impartial framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should ensure coverage does not systematically favor a political or ideological perspective; internal review should examine whether framing, sourcing, and selection reflect bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and corrective action are essential to restore credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Doing nothing will 'ensure that all the journalism that The New York Times produces in the course of this conflict will remain under a dark shadow'; corrective measures can 'reverse some of the damage' to the outlet's credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond investigation, outlets should be prepared to publish findings, issue corrections or retractions if warranted, and take visible steps to address process failures to rebuild trust.
